channel.title: AI Daily News
channel.description: Daily curated AI news, 10 articles max. Curated, credible, traceable.

item.title: Kevin Weil and Bill Peebles exit OpenAI as company continues to shed ‘side quests’
item.description: Kevin Weil and Bill Peebles are leaving OpenAI as the company shuts down Sora and folds its science team, signaling a sharp pivot away from consumer moonshots toward enterprise AI.

item.title: OpenAI takes aim at Anthropic with beefed-up Codex that gives it more power over your desktop
item.description: OpenAI's agentic coding tool has gotten a major makeover, with a variety of new powers and abilities.

item.title: InsightFinder raises $15M to help companies figure out where AI agents go wrong
item.description: According to CEO Helen Gu, the biggest problem facing the industry today is not just monitoring and diagnosing where AI models go wrong — it's also diagnosing how the entire tech stack operates now that AI is part of it.

item.title: A new way to explore the web with AI Mode in Chrome
item.description: Today’s upgrades for AI Mode in Chrome transform how you interact with the web

item.title: New ways to create personalized images in the Gemini app
item.description: Nano Banana 2 now uses your personal context and Google Photos to create images that reflect your unique life.

item.title: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS: the next generation of expressive AI speech
item.description: Gemini 3.1 Flash TTS is now available across Google products.

item.title: Turn your best AI prompts into one-click tools in Chrome
item.description: Skills in Chrome let you discover, save and remix AI workflows — and repeat them instantly.

item.title: Bringing people together at AI for the Economy Forum
item.description: Google is bringing people together in Washington D.C. at our AI for the Economy Forum.

item.title: New ways to balance cost and reliability in the Gemini API
item.description: Google is introducing two new inference tiers to the Gemini API, Flex and Priority, to balance cost and latency.

item.title: Create, edit and share videos at no cost in Google Vids
item.description: New AI capabilities are coming to Google Vids, powered by Lyria 3 and Veo 3.1, like high-quality video generation at no cost and more.
